doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Erskine Hawkins's band and learning from Tuxedo Junction
summary: He names Paul Bascomb and says he learned to improvise by copying the trumpet solo on Tuxedo Junction.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: There were four or five cats out of each band. I was crazy about Joe Thomas. I don’t know. It’s funny. Did you ever hear anything about Erskine Hawkins’s band?
See, he had a great saxophone player. This cat made some great solos. I’m trying to think of his name.

Tenor. He had two great tenor players. One of the fellows ended up here in Chicago. He died not that long ago. His name was Paul [Bascomb]. He was famous for – he was executing, at that time. Paul – how could I forget him? He had this great trumpet player, and then he had the great piano player who made After Hours. The trumpet player and the saxophone player, it seemed to me like that they were brothers. I just can’t call their – I wish I had read up on this before I got into it. But we used to play the trumpet player’s solo all the time. That’s how I almost learned how to improvise.
Actually, that’s one of my questions.
Because this solo was famous. Tuxedo Junction. It was like a story.
So you learned it from the record, then.
